mainTopic: Exile as kindness, and why אדם הראשון was created alone, last, and from dust of the whole world
overview: This amud finishes the drashos on the names of יכניה's descendants: שאלתיאל's miraculous birth, God undoing His oath, and זרובבל, who was really נחמיה בן חכליה. Next comes a story. After some wine at רבי's table, רבי חייא's sons say that משיח will not come until the houses of the ראש גולה and the נשיא come to an end. רבי חייא defends them with the line 'wine goes in, a secret comes out.' The גמרא then explains that God hurried the exile as a kindness. The exile of צדקיהו came while the Torah scholars of יכניה's exile were still alive, and according to עולא it came two years before ונושנתם. The גמרא then returns to the משנה and brings ברייתות about why אדם was created alone, why every face is different, and why people differ in voice, looks and mind. It also explains why אדם was created on ערב שבת, using the feast in משלי 9. The amud ends with רבי מאיר teaching that אדם's dust was gathered from the whole world. A new statement of רב אושעיא begins at the very end and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: שאלתיאל's mother conceived while standing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its first explanation of the name שאלתיאל. His mother conceived in an unusual way: while standing.
steps.simpleTranslation: And she (שאלתיאל's mother) conceived while standing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a drasha it started earlier on the name שאלתיאל. It points out that his birth came about in an unusual, miraculous way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is that שאלתיאל was born in a way nature does not normally allow. This miracle is part of the drasha on his name.

phrases.english: and she conceived while standing.
phrases.notes: 'She' is שאלתיאל's mother. Just before this, the גמרא said a woman normally cannot conceive standing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a drasha from the previous part of the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שאלתיאל's conception was miraculous, since his mother conceived while standing.

steps.title: A second meaning of the name שאלתיאל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers another reading of שאלתיאל: God 'asked' to undo His oath.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: שאלתיאל means that God asked about His oath, to have it undone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different explanation of the name שאלתיאל. It breaks the name into pieces that hint at God undoing His oath.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The name is split into שאל (asked), אלה (oath), and אל (God). The idea is that God, so to speak, released Himself from His oath so that יכניה could have children.

keyTerms.meaning: asked (here: asked to have an oath undone)

phrases.english: Another explanation: Shealtiel —
that God asked about His oath.
phrases.notes: It's wordplay: שאל + אלה + אל. God had sworn יכניה would be childless, and here He 'asks' to be let out of that oath.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, independent reading of the same name.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The name שאלתיאל hints that God released His oath and let יכניה have a son.

steps.title: זרובבל means sown in בבל
steps.stepSummary: The name זרובבל is read as 'planted in בבל'.
steps.simpleTranslation: זרובבל: he was 'sown' (conceived) in בבל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next name in the family line, זרובבל, and explains what it means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The name splits into זרע (seed, sown) and בבל. It tells us he was conceived in the exile in Babylonia.

phrases.english: Zerubbabel — that he was sown in Babylonia.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the drashos on the names of יכניה's descendants.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: זרובבל is a descriptive name meaning 'conceived in בבל'.

steps.title: What was his real name
steps.stepSummary: Since זרובבל is only a description, the גמרא asks what his actual name was.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what was his (real) name?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question. If זרובבל just describes where he was conceived, what was his true name? This sets up the next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the name has been read as a description, it sounds more like a nickname than a real name. So the גמרא wants to know his actual identity.

phrases.english: And what was his name?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks a follow-up question that comes out of the reading of זרובבל.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The true name of the person called זרובבל.

steps.title: His real name was נחמיה בן חכליה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that זרובבל is the same person as נחמיה בן חכליה.
steps.simpleTranslation: נחמיה בן חכליה was his name.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: זרובבל's real name was נחמיה בן חכליה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This joins two figures from the return to Israel into one person. זרובבל was his descriptive name, and נחמיה was his real one.

keyTerms.meaning: Nehemiah son of Hachaliah, a leader of the return from בבל

steps.whatToRemember: שאלתיאל and זרובבל are names that teach a lesson: a miraculous birth, God undoing His oath, and a child conceived in בבל. זרובבל was really נחמיה בן חכליה.

phrases.english: Nehemiah son of Hachaliah was his name.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 4.

steps.title: רבי gives רבי חייא's silent sons wine
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא's sons sit quietly at רבי's meal, so רבי has them given more wine so they will speak.
steps.simpleTranslation: יהודה and חזקיה, the sons of רבי חייא, were sitting at a meal before רבי and saying nothing. He said (to the servants): Give the young men a lot of wine so they will say something.
steps.whatsHappening: A new story begins. רבי wants his quiet guests to share some Torah, so he has them given wine. This sets up what they say next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story leads into a surprising statement made under the influence of wine. It also sets up רבי חייא's later defense, which is all about wine.

keyTerms.meaning: give them a lot of wine

phrases.english: Yehuda and Chizkiya, the sons of Rabbi Chiya,
were sitting at a meal before Rebbi,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא הֲווֹ קָא אָמְרִי וְלָא מִידֵּי.
phrases.english: and they were not saying anything at all.
He said to them:
phrases.notes: He's talking to his servants, not to the two sons.

phrases.english: Give the young men a lot of wine
so that they will say something.

steps.triggerLanguage: יְהוּדָה וְחִזְקִיָּה בְּנֵי רַבִּי חִיָּיא הֲווֹ יָתְבִי בִּסְעוּדְתָּא קַמֵּי רַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story about the sons of רבי חייא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Story setup: רבי gives the silent sons wine so they will speak.

steps.title: משיח will not come until two leading houses end
steps.stepSummary: Once drunk, the sons say that בן דוד will not come until the houses of the ראש גולה and the נשיא come to an end, and they bring a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once they were drunk, they began and said: בן דוד will not come until two family houses in Israel come to an end: the ראש גולה in בבל and the נשיא in Eretz Yisrael. As it says: 'He will be a sanctuary, but a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense to both houses of Israel.'
steps.whatsHappening: Now loosened up by the wine, the sons say something bold. The two ruling families, one of which is רבי's own, stand in the way of the redemption.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They read 'two houses of Israel' in the פסוק as the two leadership families: the ראש גולה and the נשיא. Their claim is that משיח will come only once these leaderships end. Saying this at the table of the נשיא himself was very daring.

keyTerms.meaning: the son of David, meaning משיח
head of the exile, leader of the Jews in בבל
the Prince, leader of the Jews in Eretz Yisrael

phrases.english: Once they became drunk, they opened up and said:
The son of David will not come

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁיִּכְלוּ שְׁנֵי בָּתֵּי אָבוֹת מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל,
phrases.english: until two family houses come to an end from Israel,
and these are they: the head of the exile in Babylonia
and the Nasi in Eretz Yisrael,
as it says: 'And he will be for a sanctuary,'
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 8:14

phrases.english: 'and for a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense'
'to both houses of Israel.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the result of the wine: the sons' bold statement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משיח will not come until the houses of the ראש גולה and the נשיא end, based on ישעיהו 8:14.

steps.title: רבי objects: thorns in my eyes
steps.stepSummary: רבי protests that they are hurting him by saying this about his own family.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: My children, are you throwing thorns into my eyes?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי objects to what the sons said, since it attacks his own position as נשיא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Thorns in my eyes' means 'you are hurting me.' רבי takes their words as a painful insult to his family's leadership.

phrases.english: He said to them: My children,
are you throwing thorns into my eyes?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts to and protests the sons' statement.
steps.kashyaTarget: The sons' statement about the two houses, said in front of the נשיא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Saying that רבי's family is holding back משיח, in his presence, is hurtful and disrespectful.

steps.title: רבי חייא: when wine goes in, secrets come out
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא defends his sons: the wine made them reveal a hidden truth, as shown by a גימטריא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא said to him: רבי, don't take it badly. 'Wine' (יין) adds up to seventy, and 'secret' (סוד) adds up to seventy. When wine goes in, a secret comes out.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא calms רבי down. He explains that the wine is what made his sons say it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יין and סוד both add up to 70 in גימטריא, which shows the link between them: wine draws out hidden things. So the sons were not trying to insult anyone; the wine simply brought out a secret they knew.

keyTerms.meaning: don't let it be bad in your eyes, don't be upset

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiya said to him: Rebbi,
do not be upset by this.
'Wine' was given in letters of seventy,
phrases.notes: י=10, י=10, ן=50, so יין adds up to 70.

phrases.english: and 'secret' was given in letters of seventy.
phrases.notes: ס=60, ו=6, ד=4, so סוד also adds up to 70.

phrases.english: Wine goes in, a secret comes out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי's protest.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframing the behavior: the words came out because of wine, not disrespect.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The sons meant to insult רבי's family.
steps.terutzMaskana: Wine brings out hidden truths, so the statement was a 'secret' that slipped out, not an insult.
steps.whatToRemember: נכנס יין יצא סוד: wine and secret both add up to 70, and wine draws out what is hidden.

steps.title: How can God's righteousness explain bringing evil
steps.stepSummary: מרי בר מר asks about a פסוק in דניאל: why would God's being righteous be the reason He hurried the evil onto us?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said in the name of מר עוקבא (some say רב חסדא said): מרי בר מר taught: What does it mean when it says, 'And ה׳ hurried the evil and brought it upon us, for ה׳ our God is righteous'? Is it because ה׳ is righteous that He hurried the evil onto us?
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins with a puzzle in a פסוק. The פסוק seems to say God brought disaster because He is righteous, which sounds strange. This sets up the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'כי' (because) seems to make God's righteousness the reason for the evil. The question is how righteousness could cause harm to come faster.

keyTerms.meaning: what is meant by what is written

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the question doubts that God is righteous. It is only asking how His righteousness can be the reason for hurrying the disaster.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר מָר עוּקְבָא,
phrases.english: Rav Chisda said that Mar Ukva said,
and some say Rav Chisda said:
Mari bar Mar taught:
What is meant by what is written: 'And ה׳ hurried the evil'
phrases.notes: דניאל 9:14

phrases.english: 'and brought it upon us,'
'for ה׳ our God is righteous'?
Because ה׳ is righteous —
'ה׳ hurried the evil and brought it upon us'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new teaching about exile, linked by topic to the ראש גולה and בבל.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How God's righteousness explains His hurrying the disaster of exile.

steps.title: Hastening צדקיהו's exile was a kindness
steps.stepSummary: Yes: God did Israel a kindness by bringing the exile of צדקיהו early, while the exiles of יכניה were still alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes. The Holy One, Blessed be He, did a kindness with Israel by bringing the exile of צדקיהו early, while the exile of יכניה was still alive.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer: the 'hurrying' really was an act of kindness. It sent the second group of exiles into a community that was already there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier exile under יכניה had already set up a living community in בבל. By bringing צדקיהו's exile while that community still existed, God made sure the new exiles had people to receive and guide them. So the speed itself was the kindness.
steps.whatToRemember: Even in punishment there was kindness: the second exile came while the first exile's community was still alive to help the newcomers.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a pattern: even when God punishes, the timing is arranged with mercy.

phrases.english: Yes, a kindness was done
by the Holy One, Blessed be He, with Israel,
in that He brought the exile of Zedekiah early
while the exile of Jeconiah was still in existence.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין, צְדָקָה עָשָׂה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עִם יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 10 by agreeing with its wording and explaining it.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The hurrying was itself righteous: צדקיהו's exile came while יכניה's exiles were still there to support them.

steps.title: The exiles of יכניה were a thousand great Torah scholars
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק about the exile of יכניה describes 'the craftsmen and the smiths, a thousand.' The גמרא reads these words as describing Torah scholars.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written about the exile of יכניה: 'The craftsmen and the smiths, a thousand.' 'Craftsman': once they opened their mouths, everyone became like deaf-mutes. 'Smith': once they closed a discussion of הלכה, nobody reopened it. How many were there? A thousand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the last answer. It shows from a פסוק that the people exiled with יכניה were great Torah scholars who were still alive when צדקיהו's exile came.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words חרש and מסגר are read as wordplay. חָרָשׁ (craftsman) sounds like חֵרֵשׁ, a deaf-mute: everyone went silent and listened when these scholars taught. מסגר means closing: when they finished a הלכה, it was settled and nobody needed to reopen it. This explains why it was a kindness to bring the next exile while these scholars were still alive.

keyTerms.meaning: The earlier exile, when King יכניה and the leaders were taken to בבל
Craftsman, read here as related to חֵרֵשׁ, a deaf-mute
Smith, read here as 'one who closes'

phrases.english: As it is written about it, in the exile of יכניה:
"The craftsmen and the smiths, a thousand."
phrases.notes: מלכים ב 24:16

phrases.english: "Craftsman": once they open their mouths,
everyone becomes like deaf-mutes.
phrases.notes: It's wordplay: חָרָשׁ sounds like חֵרֵשׁ, a deaf-mute, so everyone sat silently and listened.

phrases.english: "Smith": once they close a discussion of הלכה,
no one opens it again.
And how many were they? A thousand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in step 11 by showing who the exiles of יכניה were
steps.raayaObject: That the exiles of יכניה, still alive at צדקיהו's exile, were great Torah scholars
steps.raayaSupportSource: מלכים ב 24:16, 'הֶחָרָשׁ וְהַמַּסְגֵּר אֶלֶף', read as wordplay

steps.title: עולא: God brought the exile two years early
steps.stepSummary: עולא gives a different explanation of the kindness: God brought the exile two years before the time hinted at by the word ונושנתם.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא says: The kindness was that God brought the exile two years before ונושנתם.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא offers a second answer to מרי בר מר's question about why God's righteousness led Him to hurry the evil.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in דברים warns that after 'ונושנתם' ('you will have been in the land a long time') the people will be destroyed. The letters of ונושנתם add up to 852, but God sent them into exile at 850. Coming early meant the harshest part of the warning, total destruction, did not come true.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And you will have been long in the land' (דברים 4:25); its letters equal 852

steps.confusionAlert: עולא is not saying the exile was a good thing. He is saying that bringing it early was a kindness, because waiting the full 852 years would have brought complete destruction.

phrases.english: עולא said: that He brought it earlier
by two years before "ונושנתם."
phrases.notes: דברים 4:25. The letters of ונושנתם add up to 852, and the exile came in year 850.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, different answer to the question of step 10
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What kindness God did by hurrying the evil (from step 10)
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He brought the exile two years before the 852 years hinted at in ונושנתם, which saved Israel from total destruction

steps.title: God's 'soon' means 852 years
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב learns from עולא's explanation that when God says 'soon,' it can mean 852 years.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said: Learn from this that the 'soon' of the Master of the World is 852 years.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר יעקב draws a side lesson from what עולא just said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same פסוק in דברים says 'you will soon perish.' Since the time intended was 852 years, 'soon' from God's point of view means 852 years. Time looks very different from God's side than from ours.
steps.whatToRemember: The exile was a kindness in two ways. It came while the scholars of יכניה's exile were still alive, and it came two years early, before total destruction. God's 'soon' can mean 852 years.

phrases.english: רב אחא בר יעקב said:
Learn from this that the "soon" of the Master of the World
phrases.notes: The same פסוק says 'you will soon perish' (דברים 4:26).

phrases.english: is eight hundred and fifty-two years.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from עולא's answer in step 13
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In God's language, 'soon' can mean 852 years

steps.title: Why was אדם created alone?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה's line 'therefore' and brings a ברייתא that asks why אדם was created as a single person.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says 'Therefore...' The Rabbis taught: אדם was created alone, and for what reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and opens a new topic. This step sets up the question, and the next steps give the answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה had said that God created אדם alone and gave reasons for this. Now a ברייתא asks the same question again and gives more reasons, which come in the next two steps.

keyTerms.meaning: Therefore (quoting the opening word of the משנה's line)

phrases.english: "Therefore," etc.
phrases.notes: The גמרא is pointing back to the משנה's line, 'Therefore אדם was created alone.'

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: אדם was created alone,
and for what reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the aggadah about the exile and returns to the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason אדם was created as a single person

steps.title: So heretics cannot claim there are many powers in heaven
steps.stepSummary: The first answer is that if many people had been created at once, heretics could claim each was made by a different god.
steps.simpleTranslation: So that heretics would not say, 'There are many powers in heaven.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives its first reason why אדם was created alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If several first humans had been made, heretics could say that each one came from a different creator. Starting all of humanity from one person shows there is one Creator.

phrases.english: So that heretics will not say:
"There are many powers in heaven."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: To prevent the heretical claim that there are many gods

steps.title: So nobody can blame or credit their ancestry
steps.stepSummary: A second reason: because everyone comes from one person, neither the righteous nor the wicked can say their family made them that way.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: because of the righteous and because of the wicked. So the righteous will not say, 'We are children of a righteous man,' and the wicked will not say, 'We are children of a wicked man.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a second, different reason why אדם was created alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If there had been a righteous first father and a wicked first father, people could blame or credit their roots. The righteous might think they need no effort, and the wicked might think they cannot change. Since everyone comes from the same single person, each person is responsible for their own choices.

phrases.aramaic: דָּבָר אַחֵר: מִפְּנֵי הַצַּדִּיקִים וּמִפְּנֵי הָרְשָׁעִים,
phrases.english: Another explanation: because of the righteous and because of the wicked,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא יְהוּ הַצַּדִּיקִים אוֹמְרִים ״אָנוּ בְּנֵי צַדִּיק״,
phrases.english: so that the righteous will not say, "We are the children of a righteous man,"
and the wicked will not say, "We are the children of a wicked man."

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר אַחֵר: מִפְּנֵי הַצַּדִּיקִים וּמִפְּנֵי הָרְשָׁעִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the same question from step 15
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: So that nobody can credit or blame their ancestry for their righteousness or wickedness

steps.title: Third reason: so families will not fight over whose ancestor was greater
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא gives another reason for creating one person: so families would not quarrel about their ancestry. It backs this up with a קל וחומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: he was created alone because of the families, so families would not fight with each other. Even now, when only one person was created, they fight. If two had been created, they would fight even more!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds a third reason why אדם הראשון was created alone: to stop families from fighting about whose ancestor was better.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If humanity came from two founders, each family could boast that its founder was greater. Since everyone shares one ancestor, that argument has no basis. The ברייתא admits families still fight today, and argues that with two founders it would be far worse.

keyTerms.meaning: Another explanation; introduces an additional reason
All the more so; the closing words of a קל וחומר

phrases.english: Another explanation: because of the families,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא יְהוּ מִשְׁפָּחוֹת מִתְגָּרוֹת זוֹ בָּזוֹ.
phrases.english: so that families should not quarrel with one another.
And if now, when he was created alone, they still quarrel,

phrases.aramaic: נִבְרְאוּ שְׁנַיִם – עַל אַחַת כַּמָּה וְכַמָּה!
phrases.english: had two been created, all the more so!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third answer to the question in step 15, after the answers in steps 16 and 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: One founder prevents families from fighting over whose ancestor was greater.

steps.title: Fourth reason: to reduce robbery
steps.stepSummary: Another reason: because of robbers and those who take by force. Even with one founder people rob, and with two founders they would rob even more.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: because of robbers and those who take things by force. Even now, when only one person was created, people rob and take by force. If two had been created, they would do it even more!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a fourth reason why אדם הראשון was created alone: to cut down on robbery.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When everyone knows they come from the same single ancestor, people feel like one family, and this holds back stealing. The ברייתא uses the same קל וחומר pattern as in step 18: robbery happens even now, and with two founders it would be worse.

keyTerms.meaning: People who take by force or pressure, sometimes leaving payment

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא gives four reasons for creating one אדם: against heretics, against family excuses, against family rivalry, and against robbery.

phrases.english: Another explanation: because of the robbers
and because of those who take by force.

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה עַכְשָׁו שֶׁנִּבְרָא יְחִידִי גּוֹזְלִין וְחוֹמְסִין,
phrases.english: And if now, when he was created alone, people rob and take by force,

phrases.aramaic: נִבְרְאוּ שְׁנַיִם – עַל אַחַת כַּמָּה וְכַמָּה!
phrases.english: had two been created, all the more so!

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר אַחֵר: מִפְּנֵי הַגַּזְלָנִין וּמִפְּנֵי הַחַמְסָנִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fourth and final answer in the ברייתא's list, using the same pattern as step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: One shared ancestor makes people feel like family, which reduces robbery.

steps.title: God's greatness: many people from one seal, yet none are alike
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's next phrase about God's greatness and brings a ברייתא. A human seal makes identical coins, but God makes every person from אדם הראשון's seal and each one is different. A פסוק in איוב supports this.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And to tell His greatness, etc.' The Rabbis taught: This shows the greatness of the King of kings, הקדוש ברוך הוא. A person stamps many coins with one seal and they all look the same. But הקדוש ברוך הוא stamps every person with the seal of אדם הראשון, and not one looks like another. As the פסוק says: 'It is changed like clay under the seal, and they stand like a garment.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה, 'to tell the greatness of God,' and brings a ברייתא that explains it with a parable about coins and a seal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A seal in human hands can only repeat one image. God starts from one 'seal,' אדם הראשון, yet produces endless different faces, which shows His power. The פסוק describes people pressed from a seal like clay, yet looking as different as garments.

phrases.english: The משנה said: 'And to tell His greatness, etc.'
The Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: לְהַגִּיד גְּדוּלָּתוֹ שֶׁל מֶלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים
phrases.english: To tell the greatness of the supreme King of kings,
the Holy One, Blessed be He,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאָדָם טוֹבֵעַ כַּמָּה מַטְבְּעוֹת בְּחוֹתָם אֶחָד
phrases.english: for a person stamps several coins with one seal
and they all look like one another,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא טוֹבֵעַ כׇּל אָדָם
phrases.english: but the Holy One, Blessed be He, stamps every person
with the seal of Adam the first man
and not one of them looks like another,
as it is said: 'It is changed like clay under the seal
phrases.notes: איוב 38:14

phrases.english: and they stand like a garment.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the list of reasons and moves to the next phrase of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Creating all people from one founder, yet each unique, shows God's greatness beyond any human craftsman.

steps.title: Why do faces differ from one another?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks what purpose there is in making every face different.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why are their faces not like one another?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks a follow-up question: why did God make every face different? It is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 20 said that different faces show God's greatness. Now the ברייתא asks for a practical purpose for these differences in daily life.

phrases.english: And for what reason are their faces not
similar to one another?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִפְּנֵי מָה אֵין פַּרְצוּפֵיהֶן דּוֹמִין זֶה לָזֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on step 20's point that no two people look alike.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical purpose of people having different faces.

steps.title: So no one can falsely claim another's house or wife
steps.stepSummary: Different faces stop a person from seeing a nice house or a beautiful woman and claiming 'It's mine.' A פסוק in איוב supports this.
steps.simpleTranslation: So that a person should not see a nice home and a beautiful woman and say: 'She is mine.' As the פסוק says: 'And from the wicked their light is held back, and the raised arm will be broken.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers: if everyone looked alike, a dishonest man could claim someone else's home or wife as his own, and nobody could prove him wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Different faces let people identify who really owns a home and who a woman's husband is. The פסוק, which comes right after the 'seal' פסוק, shows that the purpose is to stop the wicked from carrying out their plans.

keyTerms.meaning: A raised arm, meaning the power of the wicked

phrases.english: So that a person will not see a nice home
or a beautiful woman and say: 'She is mine.'
As it is said: 'And from the wicked their light is withheld
phrases.notes: איוב 38:15

phrases.english: and the raised arm shall be broken.'

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁלֹּא יִרְאֶה אָדָם דִּירָה נָאָה וְאִשָּׁה נָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Different faces stop wicked people from falsely claiming others' homes or wives.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: people differ in voice, looks, and mind
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר teaches that people differ in three ways: voice, appearance, and mind. Voice and appearance differ to prevent forbidden relationships, and minds differ to protect against robbers.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: רבי מאיר used to say: A person differs from another in three things: in voice, in appearance, and in mind. In voice and appearance, because of forbidden relationships. In mind, because of robbers and those who take by force.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא in which רבי מאיר lists three ways people differ, and gives a reason for each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If voices and looks were the same, a man could not recognize his own wife and might come to a forbidden relationship. If everyone thought the same way, robbers could guess where others hide their valuables. So each difference protects people from a specific danger.
steps.whatToRemember: Human differences are not random: different faces and voices protect marriages and property, and different minds protect against robbers.

phrases.english: It is taught: Rabbi Meir would say:
In three things a person differs from another:
in voice, in appearance, and in mind.
In voice and appearance, because of forbidden relationships,
and in mind, because of robbers and those who take by force.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens the theme of steps 20-22 from faces alone to voice, appearance, and mind.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: People differ in voice and appearance to prevent forbidden relationships, and in mind to protect against robbers.

steps.title: אדם was created on ערב שבת
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא states that אדם הראשון was created on ערב שבת, the last day of creation.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: אדם was created on ערב שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא that says אדם הראשון was created on Friday, right before the first שבת. This sets up the question of why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier steps were about why all people come from one person. Now the topic moves to when that one person was created. Man was the last creation, made after everything else.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Adam was created on Shabbat eve,

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אָדָם נִבְרָא בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from how people differ from each other to when the first person was created.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אדם הראשון was created last, on ערב שבת.

steps.title: Why was אדם created then?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks why אדם הראשון was created specifically on ערב שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for what reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks a simple question: why was man created on the last day? This sets up a list of answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a real question looking for a reason, not an attack. Several answers follow: the first begins 'שֶׁלֹּא יְהוּ מִינִים', and each one after it starts with דבר אחר.

phrases.english: And for what reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the statement in step 24.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The purpose of creating man on ערב שבת.

steps.title: So no one can say man helped create the world
steps.stepSummary: Man was created last so the מינים could not claim he was God's partner in creation.
steps.simpleTranslation: So that heretics should not say: The Holy One, Blessed be He, had a partner in the work of creation.
steps.whatsHappening: The first answer: if man had been there earlier, people could claim he helped God create. Since he came last, he clearly took no part in it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everything else was already finished before man existed. That proves God created the world alone.

phrases.english: So that heretics should not say:

phrases.aramaic: שׁוּתָּף הָיָה לוֹ לְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, had a partner
phrases.notes: The 'partner' they would point to is Adam himself.

phrases.english: in the work of creation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question in step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Creating man last prevents the claim that God had a partner in creation.

steps.title: Even a mosquito came before you
steps.stepSummary: Second reason: if a person becomes proud, he can be reminded that even a mosquito was created before him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: if a person becomes arrogant, one says to him: A mosquito came before you in the work of creation.
steps.whatsHappening: A second answer: being created last keeps people humble. A proud person can be told that even a tiny bug was made before him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first answer was about God's honor. This answer is about human character. Coming last becomes a reason for humility.

keyTerms.meaning: he becomes arrogant, his mind gets puffed up

phrases.aramaic: דָּבָר אַחֵר: שֶׁאִם תָּזוּחַ דַּעְתּוֹ עָלָיו,
phrases.english: Another explanation: that if he becomes arrogant,
one says to him: A mosquito came before you
in the work of creation.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר אַחֵר: שֶׁאִם תָּזוּחַ דַּעְתּוֹ עָלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, separate answer to the same question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Being created last keeps man humble.

steps.title: To go straight into a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: Third reason: man was created right before שבת so he could start keeping a מצוה immediately.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: so that he could enter into the מצוה right away.
steps.whatsHappening: A third answer: since man was created just before שבת, his very first act could be doing a מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer is positive: being created last means the first thing man does is serve God. There is no waiting time before his first מצוה.

phrases.aramaic: דָּבָר אַחֵר: כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּכָּנֵס לַמִּצְוָה מִיָּד.
phrases.english: Another explanation: so that he could enter into the מצוה immediately.
phrases.notes: The מצוה meant here is keeping שבת, which started right after he was created.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר אַחֵר: כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּכָּנֵס לַמִּצְוָה מִיָּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third, separate answer to the same question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: So man could immediately keep the מצוה of שבת.

steps.title: Like guests invited to a ready feast
steps.stepSummary: Fourth reason: man was created last so the whole world would be ready for him, like a king who invites guests only after the palace and meal are prepared.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: so that he could enter the feast right away. It is like a human king who built palaces, finished them, prepared a feast, and only then brought in the guests.
steps.whatsHappening: A fourth answer, with a parable: God first prepared everything man would need, and only then brought man in, like a host who sets the table before guests arrive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here coming last is a sign of honor, not lowliness. The world is the 'feast' and man is the invited guest. This answer is then supported by a פסוק in the next step.

phrases.aramaic: דָּבָר אַחֵר: כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּכָּנֵס לַסְּעוּדָה מִיָּד.
phrases.english: Another explanation: so that he could enter the feast immediately.
It is like a king of flesh and blood
who built palaces and finished them,
and prepared a feast,
and only afterward brought in guests.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר אַחֵר: כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּכָּנֵס לַסְּעוּדָה מִיָּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A fourth answer to the same question, explained through a parable.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Man came last so he could enjoy a world already fully prepared for him.

steps.title: The פסוק about Wisdom's house and feast
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא quotes משלי 9:1-3, about Wisdom building a house, preparing a meal, and calling guests, as support for the feast parable.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'Wisdom built her house, she carved out her seven pillars. She slaughtered her meat, she mixed her wine, she also set her table. She sent out her maidens, she calls out upon the heights of the city.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings a פסוק that matches the parable: first a house is built, then food is prepared, and only then are guests called in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The order in the פסוק (house, food, then inviting) matches the order of the parable. The next step explains each part of the פסוק as a stage of creation.

phrases.english: As it says: 'Wisdom built her house,
phrases.notes: משלי 9:1-3

phrases.english: she carved out her seven pillars.
She slaughtered her meat, she mixed her wine,
she also set her table.
She sent out her maidens, she calls out
upon the heights of the city.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a פסוק to support the feast parable of step 29.
steps.raayaObject: The idea that the world was fully prepared before man was brought in.

steps.title: Reading the פסוק as the story of creation
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains each part of the פסוק: the house is the world built with wisdom, the seven pillars are the seven days of creation, the meal is the seas, rivers and all the world's needs, and the invited guests are אדם and חוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Wisdom built her house': this is the way of the Holy One, Blessed be He, Who created the whole world with wisdom. 'She carved out her seven pillars': these are the seven days of creation. 'She slaughtered her meat, she mixed her wine, she also set her table': these are the seas, rivers, and all the needs of the world. 'She sent out her maidens, she calls out': this is אדם and חוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא goes through the פסוק piece by piece and matches each part to a stage of creation, ending with man as the one invited in at the end.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows how the פסוק proves the point: everything in the world (the 'meal') was ready before אדם and חוה were brought in. Man being last means he is the honored guest.
steps.whatToRemember: Man was created last for four reasons: so no one says he helped create, to keep him humble, to start with a מצוה right away, and to walk into a world already prepared for him like a guest at a feast.

phrases.english: 'Wisdom built her house' –

phrases.aramaic: זוֹ מִידָּתוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא,
phrases.english: this is the way of the Holy One, Blessed be He,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁבָּרָא אֶת כָּל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ בְּחׇכְמָה.
phrases.english: Who created the entire world with wisdom.
'She carved out her seven pillars' –
these are the seven days of creation.

phrases.aramaic: ״טָבְחָה טִבְחָהּ מָסְכָה יֵינָהּ אַף עָרְכָה שֻׁלְחָנָהּ״ –
phrases.english: 'She slaughtered her meat, she mixed her wine, she also set her table' –

phrases.aramaic: אֵלּוּ יַמִּים וּנְהָרוֹת וְכׇל צוֹרְכֵי עוֹלָם.
phrases.english: these are the seas and rivers and all the needs of the world.
'She sent out her maidens, she calls out' –
this is Adam and Eve.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״חׇכְמוֹת בָּנְתָה בֵיתָהּ״ – זוֹ מִידָּתוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how each phrase of the פסוק in step 30 matches the story of creation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק describes creation in order, with אדם and חוה brought in last into a ready world.

steps.title: Two פסוקים: on the heights or on a seat?
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה points out that one פסוק says 'upon the heights' (על גפי) and another says 'on a seat' (על כסא), which seem to contradict.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Upon the heights of the city': רבה בר בר חנה raised a contradiction. It is written 'upon the heights,' and it is written 'on a seat.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא picks up the last words of the פסוק and brings רבה בר בר חנה, who notices that a later פסוק in the same chapter describes the place differently. This sets up an answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this reading the פסוק is about man. One פסוק places him 'upon the heights' and another places him 'on a seat.' Which is it?

keyTerms.meaning: he raised a contradiction (between two sources)
upon the heights, on top of

phrases.english: 'Upon the heights of the city' –
Rabba bar bar Ḥana raised a contradiction:
It is written 'upon the heights,'
and it is written 'on a seat.'
phrases.notes: This is from משלי 9:14, a few פסוקים later in the same chapter.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה רָמֵי: כְּתִיב ״עַל גַּפֵּי״, וּכְתִיב ״עַל כִּסֵּא״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the last phrase of the פסוק and sets it against another פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording 'על גפי' in משלי 9:3 compared with 'על כסא' in משלי 9:14.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two פסוקים seem to describe the same place in two different ways.

steps.title: First on the heights, later on a seat
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה answers that both are true at different times: at first 'upon the heights,' and later 'on a seat.'
steps.simpleTranslation: At first, upon the heights; in the end, on a seat.
steps.whatsHappening: The contradiction is resolved by time: each פסוק describes a different stage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two פסוקים do not argue; they describe a before and an after. At first אדם was alone 'upon the heights,' and later, once חוה was paired with him, he sat 'on a seat,' like a groom's seat.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think one פסוק is 'wrong.' Both are right; they just describe two different times.

phrases.english: At first – upon the heights,
and in the end – on a seat.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּתְּחִלָּה – עַל גַּפֵּי, וּלְבַסּוֹף – עַל כִּסֵּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 32.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two פסוקים seem to describe the same moment in two conflicting ways.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'על גפי' describes the beginning and 'על כסא' describes later, so there is no contradiction.

steps.title: Who lured him? The woman told him
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains משלי 9:4 as God asking who led this man to sin, with the answer that a woman told him to.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'Whoever is thoughtless, let him turn in here; as for him that lacks understanding, she tells him.' הקדוש ברוך הוא said: Who lured this one? A woman told him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps explaining the משלי פסוקים from the feast parable, now reading the next פסוק as a comment on why the man sinned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word פתי (thoughtless) is read like פיתהו (lured him), turning it into the question 'who lured him?' The words אמרה לו (she told him) supply the answer: a woman told him. Since the guests at the feast were אדם and חוה, this fits the man being led to sin by the woman.

keyTerms.meaning: A thoughtless or easily misled person
The Holy One, Blessed be He

phrases.english: "Whoever is thoughtless, let him turn in here;
as for him that lacks understanding, she tells him."
phrases.notes: משלי 9:4, the next פסוק after the feast פסוקים from before.

phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said:
Who lured this one?
phrases.notes: This plays on the word פתי, reading it as 'who lured (פיתה) him?'

phrases.english: A woman told him.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי פֶתִי יָסֻר הֵנָּה חֲסַר לֵב אָמְרָה לּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the line-by-line explanation of the משלי פסוקים from step 31, moving on to the next פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The man who 'lacks understanding' was led astray because a woman told him to sin.

steps.title: Proof that one led by a woman lacks understanding
steps.stepSummary: Another פסוק in משלי calls a man who sins with a woman 'lacking understanding,' supporting the reading in step 34.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'He who commits adultery with a woman lacks understanding.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק showing that the phrase 'lacks understanding' is tied to a man who sins because of a woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 34 linked 'lacks understanding' to a man led astray by a woman. This פסוק uses the exact same words, חסר לב, for a man who sins with a woman, so the link is backed up by the language of משלי itself.

phrases.english: As it is written:
"He who commits adultery with a woman lacks understanding."
phrases.notes: משלי 6:32. The same words חסר לב show up in both פסוקים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the reading of step 34 by matching the phrase חסר לב in another פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: The reading that 'lacks understanding' refers to a man led to sin by a woman.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משלי 6:32, which uses חסר לב for one who sins with a woman.
steps.whatToRemember: This closes the feast parable: the world was prepared like a palace and a meal, אדם and חוה were the invited guests, and the man was led to sin when the woman told him to.

steps.title: אדם הראשון was formed from dust of the whole world
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר teaches that the dust used to form אדם הראשון was gathered from all over the world.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי מאיר used to say: The dust of אדם הראשון was gathered from the entire world.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא in which רבי מאיר teaches where the dust for אדם הראשון came from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new teaching about how the first man was made. אדם was not formed from one spot of earth. His dust was collected from the whole world.

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Meir would say:
Adam, the first man:
from the entire world
his dust was gathered,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about how אדם הראשון was formed, after the feast parable is finished.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dust that formed אדם הראשון was gathered from the entire world.

steps.title: Two פסוקים prove the dust came from everywhere
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר joins a פסוק saying God's eyes saw אדם's unshaped form with a פסוק saying God's eyes roam the whole earth.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is said: 'Your eyes saw my unshaped form,' and it is written: 'For the eyes of ה׳ roam throughout the whole earth.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר proves his teaching by putting two פסוקים about God's 'eyes' side by side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק says God's eyes saw the unshaped body of the first man. The second says God's eyes roam over the whole earth. Put together, the unshaped body was made from what God's eyes look over, which is the whole earth.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is said (introduces a פסוק)
My unshaped form, a body not yet finished

phrases.english: as it is said: "Your eyes saw my unshaped form,"
phrases.notes: תהלים 139:16

phrases.english: and it is written: "For the eyes of the Lord roam
throughout the whole earth."
phrases.notes: דברי הימים ב 16:9. Both פסוקים mention God's 'eyes', so what His eyes saw, the unshaped body, came from the whole earth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the scriptural source for רבי מאיר's statement in step 36.
steps.raayaObject: That אדם הראשון's dust was gathered from the entire world.
steps.raayaSupportSource: תהלים 139:16 together with דברי הימים ב 16:9, linked through the word 'eyes'.
steps.confusionAlert: Neither פסוק alone says the dust came from everywhere. The proof only works when you read the two together through the shared word 'eyes'.

steps.title: רב אושעיא begins a new teaching about אדם הראשון
steps.stepSummary: רב אושעיא, quoting רב, starts a new statement about אדם הראשון that continues on the next part of the daf.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אושעיא said in the name of רב: אדם הראשון...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new teaching. It opens רב אושעיא's statement about אדם הראשון, and the rest of it continues right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a second teaching about how the first man was formed, adding detail to רבי מאיר's idea. For now, we only have the speaker and the subject, אדם הראשון.

phrases.english: Rav Oshaya said in the name of Rav:
Adam, the first man:

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אוֹשַׁעְיָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב: אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further teaching about the forming of אדם הראשון, after רבי מאיר's ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Opening of a statement about the forming of אדם הראשון; the content continues next.
